items.title: Stock Radar: SBI Cards & Payment Services stock showing signs of trend reversal after falling over 30% from highs
items.description: SBI Cards & Payment Services has shown signs of a potential trend reversal after bouncing back from key support levels. Technical indicators suggest improving momentum, with experts recommending high-risk traders consider buying the stock on dips for a target of Rs 700 in the coming weeks.

The simple average of the above-mentioned five component ratings is normally distributed to reach an average score.

items.title: Emmvee Photovoltaic among 5 stocks closed below VWAP, signalling bearish shift
items.description: On July 17, the closing prices of five stocks in the Nifty500 pack dropped more than 1.5% below their Volume Weighted Average Price (VWAP), according to StockEdge's technical scan data. A move below the VWAP suggests a potential bearish trend, as it indicates that the stock is trading below its average price for the session after accounting for trading volumes.When the closing price falls below the VWAP, it means the closing price is lower than the average price at which the stock traded throughout the day, with the average weighted by trading volume. Traders and investors often interpret this as a bearish signal, reflecting increasing selling pressure and the possibility of continued downside momentum.

items.title: Federal Bank among 5 stocks closed above VWAP, signalling bullish shift
items.description: On July 17, the closing prices of five stocks in the Nifty500 pack rallied more than 1.5% above their Volume Weighted Average Price (VWAP), according to StockEdge's technical scan data. A move above the VWAP suggests a potential bullish trend, as it indicates that the stock is trading above its average price for the session after accounting for trading volumes.When the closing price rises above the VWAP, it signifies that the closing price is higher than the average price at which the stock was traded throughout the day, with the average weighted by trading volume. Traders and investors often interpret this as a bullish signal, reflecting positive market sentiment and the possibility of continued upward momentum.

items.title: Jio Financial Services among 6 stocks showing bullish RSI upswing
items.description: On July 17, six stocks in the Nifty500 segment that gained over 2.5% were highlighted in the RSI Trending Up scan, based on data from StockEdge.com. An uptrend signal is generated when the RSI value crosses above 50 from lower levels. “RSI trending up” indicates that Relative Strength Index (RSI) values are rising, suggesting strengthening momentum in the stock’s price action. This can indicate potential upward movement and is often used by traders to identify buying opportunities in momentum-driven markets.

items.title: Nifty ready for 24,500-24,750 levels after breakout rally: Analysts
items.description: Analysts expect the rally to extend towards 24,500-24,750, with some seeing the potential for 25,000, although they believe the index must first overcome resistance around the 24,350-24,600 zone. The index closed at 24,334 on Friday.

items.title: Stocks in news: ICICI Bank, YES Bank, Kotak Bank, RIL, Axis Bank
items.description: Markets advanced Friday, gaining over one percent despite weak global cues. Analysts await quarterly results from Reliance Industries, HDFC Bank, and ICICI Bank. ICICI Bank reported a 16% year-on-year net profit increase for the June quarter. YES Bank and PNB also posted significant year-on-year profit growth. Kotak Mahindra Bank and Axis Bank also announced their first-quarter financial results.

items.title: D-St set for a negative opening as GIFT Nifty signals weak start
items.description: Domestic equities ended the week on a strong note, with Nifty rising. Analysts expect a gradual uptrend next week, driven by strong Q1 earnings. Investor focus will remain on management commentary and earnings reactions. India VIX fell, indicating reduced market fear. Foreign investors were net buyers of shares on Friday.

items.title: Carnelian Capital plans PE foray with Rs 2,000 crore fund
items.description: The investment manager, which oversees about ₹18,300 crore across portfolio management services and alternative investment funds, plans to raise the maiden fund in the next 12-18 months. It will focus on profitable companies seeking ₹100-300 crore of growth capital, a segment the firm believes has become underserved as private equity funds have grown larger.

items.title: Select mid & smallcaps on a roll, but broader market lags
items.description: Nifty Midcap 150 reached a record high, and Smallcap 250 neared its peak.  However, the broader market breadth shows a weak trend with few gainers.  Concentrated fund flows into mid and small caps are driving select indices higher.  Foreign institutional investors have exited bluechips, causing the Nifty 50 to underperform.  The market is in a consolidation phase, awaiting improved buying interest in largecaps.

items.title: Axis Bank weighs raising stake in its insurance venture to 30%
items.description: In June 2026, Axis Bank announced a further investment of up to ?381 crore in Axis Max Life Insurance, taking the combined shareholding of Axis Bank and its subsidiaries-Axis Capital and Axis Securities-from 19.02% to 19.99%. Max Financial Services holds 80.01%.

items.title: Regional conflict-driven curbs weigh on flow: FCNR(B) inflows may miss initial estimates, says HDFC Bank CEO
items.description: Expected FCNR(B) deposit inflows are now projected at fifty to fifty-five billion dollars.  Taxation complexities for nonresidents and tighter West Asian liquidity are impacting these mobilizations.  Early estimates had not fully factored in the tax impact on non-resident Indians.  The Reserve Bank of India's special incentives for this program will conclude on September thirtieth.  HDFC Bank is pursuing a three-pronged approach to maximize its deposit mobilization efforts.
